same_choices: Commit motion is an elastic scale/overshoot spring pop (both settle with an overshoot beat so 'landed' is felt, not just seen)
Un-save is a distinct reverse of the save motion rather than a second identical action
aria-pressed toggle plus prefers-reduced-motion fallback that drops the spring/overshoot to a plain fade
Saved state carries a persistent accent-colored cue that survives after the transient animation ends
Interaction is a single in-place click on one button (no gesture, button never moves position)
Un-save is the same button clicked again, running a reverse animation back to empty
Pending/in-flight state shown by an animated indeterminate indicator (breathing pulse vs seam shimmer) with optimistic commit and a failure recovery animation
Core motion carries the state change continuously and explicitly rejects an instant static filled/outline swap
Motion includes an overshoot settle for tactility
aria/reduced-motion accessibility handling with the persistent cue readable without hover or motion
Persistent saved cue is a small colored badge dot at the top-right corner/notch (near-identical; empty state has no dot)
Metaphor is containment/deposit: the item is put away into a target (shelf-slot vs pocket/pouch) rather than a page mark
Un-save is the literal inverse of the commit action
Commit motion is an elastic/overshoot settle
prefers-reduced-motion drops the overshoot to a plain fade
